clue.text: At back of motel, model poised to strip

indicators.note: model used as a verb, to shape or fashion, so these letters are moulded into a new order
the back of a word is its final letter, here the end of the hotel word

explanation.surface: A model strikes a pose behind a roadside motel before undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' poses as a person but is the anagram signal: POISED rearranged gives DESPOI, then L, the last letter of 'motel', is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or strip a place of its valuables, a synonym in the sense of stripping bare.

clue.text: Failing to go over to the other side

definitions.meaning: a failing is a flaw or shortcoming, used here as a noun

definitions.text: to go over to the other side
definitions.meaning: to desert one's country or party for the enemy or a rival

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a flaw; as a verb it means to desert to the opposing side, as spies did in the Cold War.

clue.text: Meat in ladle finally spilled — some going over head?

indicators.note: the meat word is placed within the shortened utensil word
the final letter of the utensil word spills out and is lost

parts.note: a spoon is a ladle-like utensil for serving
ham is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: Gravy from the ladle slops everywhere as someone serves the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally spilled' means the utensil loses its last letter. The definition is playful: hair wash is something poured over your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair wash is poured over the head when washing, so 'some going over head' playfully describes it.

clue.text: Those seeing outside broadcast with tennis players

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast, a programme made away from the studio
servers are tennis players putting the ball into play

explanation.surface: A TV crew films a match on location among the tennis players.
explanation.definitionFit: Observers are watchers, people who see or witness something.

clue.text: Part of a blade poorly aligned, inch under

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits under the first
something poorly done is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to inch is to edge, move forward slowly

explanation.surface: A badly lined-up blade sits an inch below where it should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges ALIGNED into LEADING; 'under' places EDGE below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading edge is the front edge of a wing, propeller or blade that meets the air first.

clue.text: In writing new page, copy is gilt-edged

indicators.note: the gold letters form the edges around the rest

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: A freshly written page, copied out, turns out to be a gilt-edged investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gilt-edged' has to be split: 'gilt' is heraldic gold and 'edged' is the container signal. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on paper is recorded in writing, an idiom for a written record.

clue.text: Fool needing bread, short of a crust?

indicators.note: losing the crust means losing the outer edge, here the first letter of the bread word

parts.note: a loaf is a portion of bread

explanation.surface: Someone so poor they lack even a crust of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of a crust' trims the leading L from LOAF.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Horse heading for pine tree

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, here the first of pine

parts.note: acer is the maple genus of trees

explanation.surface: A horse trots off towards a pine tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse trained to pace, a gait used in harness racing.

clue.text: The city buried pontiff, burying married couple deeper

indicators.note: in a down answer the couple's letters go further down, after the rest
the abbreviation for married is buried inside the pontiff word

parts.note: the pope is the pontiff
II is the Roman numeral two, a couple

explanation.surface: In an ancient city a pope is laid to rest, a married couple interred below him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burying' is the container signal; 'deeper' puts the Roman two lower in this down entry. 'The city buried' refers to the eruption of Vesuvius.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman city near Naples was buried under ash when Vesuvius erupted in AD 79.

clue.text: Into traditional main course, introduce fruit without a preliminary trial

indicators.note: the fruit, minus a letter, is introduced into the dinner word

parts.note: a roast is the traditional British Sunday main course

indicators.note: the fruit word goes without the letter a

parts.note: a date is a fruit of the palm

explanation.surface: Fruit is introduced into the classic roast dinner as a trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: DATE without A is DTE, put into ROAST to give ROA-DTE-ST. A roast dinner is the traditional British Sunday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial of a vehicle or product under real conditions before wider use.

clue.text: Colours on this plant's flower

parts.note: a flag is an iris plant; with the apostrophe s it gives the possessive
crossword 'flower' is something that flows, a river; the Taff runs through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A gardener admires the bloom on a flowering plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river here, the Taff in Wales. 'Colours' are a regimental flag, flown on the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours are a regiment's flags, and a flagpole is what they are flown on.

clue.text: Butterfly identifying place to breathe

definitions.meaning: the ... is a butterfly with a white ...-shaped mark on its wing
a punctuation mark showing where a reader may pause

explanation.definitionFit: It names a European butterfly and the punctuation mark where a reader takes a short pause.

clue.text: Lark finding shrub

definitions.meaning: a lark is a bit of fun or mischief, a prank
a Mediterranean shrub whose buds are pickled

explanation.definitionFit: It means a playful escapade, a lark, and also the prickly bush bearing pickled flower buds.

clue.text: Bury group, displaying cross

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a sect is a religious group or faction

explanation.surface: A gang from the town of Bury puts on an angry display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town and 'cross' like angry; they are the verb to inter and the verb to cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cross, as two lines that meet at a point.

clue.text: More than one radio station runs doubly vacant broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered, so the letters are spread about anew
the emptied word is used twice
vacant means emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A radio station keeps putting out programmes to an empty audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties RUNS to RS, 'doubly' makes that RSRS, and 'broadcast' scrambles it with STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Small portable radios were called transistors, after the component inside them.

clue.text: Engineer gains offer, securing just overseas business

indicators.note: the anagram holds the just word firmly inside it
to engineer is to contrive or arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: fair means just

explanation.surface: An engineer wins a job offer from a firm abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person but is the anagram signal, giving FOREIGNAFS; 'securing' holds the just word between the second F and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign affairs are a nation's dealings with other countries, business conducted overseas.

clue.text: Rich food not genuine — after cooking, I cut right through it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters run through the fake word, inside it

parts.note: fake means not genuine

indicators.note: cooked letters are mixed up, so they appear rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook slices a rich cake that turns out not to be the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cooking' rearranges the letters to RUITC; 'through it' sends them inside the word for not genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is a dense cake packed with dried fruit, a classic rich food.

clue.text: Modern philosopher gathering momentum

indicators.note: the philosopher word gathers the momentum word inside it

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, a philosopher
pace means speed, momentum

explanation.surface: A thinker gathers speed with modern ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something very modern or futuristic.

clue.text: Plans used cheap to redraft, so delighted

explanation.definitionFit: Pleased as Punch is an idiom for very delighted, after the gleeful puppet.

clue.text: Giving transaction up, credit cut

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sale is a transaction

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its end

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, buying on tick

explanation.surface: A deal goes through but the credit line is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SALE to ELAS; 'cut' docks TICK to TIC. 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means flexible, giving way under pressure, a synonym of yielding.

clue.text: Hardly how babies are born?

definitions.meaning: babies arrive with nothing on, in the bare state

clue.text: Lacking social categorization as a redundant teacher?

clue.text: Light sleeper's first to get up in the country

indicators.note: the first letter of sleeper's

clue.text: One's blooming sample hasn't a lid!

clue.text: See red shirt-like garment adorning wife, a leader of fashion

clue.text: Shady borders around church close, without a background

indicators.note: the border letters go around the church and close words
